text:
Summary:
The blog post analyses how different design choices in recent DeepMind impact-measure work (Relative Reachability, Attainable Utility Preservation, Unreachability) influence an RL agent’s incentives in five grid-world environments (Sushi, Vase, Box, Survival).  It links particular choices of baseline, deviation measure, discounting and penalty function to three classes of unwanted side-effects—interference, offsetting and magnitude-blind irreversible change—and reports empirical results that show when alternative choices successfully remove those incentives.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]

Inference-strategy justification:
The paper explicitly presents risks, mechanisms (baseline, deviation measure, discounting, penalty function), empirical findings and implied safety recommendations.  Where no explicit “intervention” label exists, I inferred the natural safety intervention (e.g. “apply RR penalty with stepwise-inaction baseline”) directly implied by the stated positive results.  All such inferences are clearly marked with edge confidence 2 and maturity 2.

Extraction completeness:
All causal paths beginning with the single top-level risk “Unintended side effects from AI agent actions in real-world deployment” and terminating in four actionable safety interventions are captured.  Each intermediate claim (baseline influence, deviation-measure influence, theoretical framing, empirical validation) appears once and connects to at least one other node, yielding a single fully connected fabric without duplicates or islands.

Key limitations:
1. Findings are limited to small grid-worlds; maturity hence rated “2”.
2. The blog post is a summary, so some mechanistic details had to be inferred at low confidence.
3. Section headers are absent; rationales therefore cite the closest descriptive paragraph (e.g. “On the Sushi environment”).

Key instruction-set improvement:
The current prompt demands citing “closest preceding section titles”, but many sources (like this blog post) lack explicit headers, forcing vague rationales.  Allowing paragraph quotations or approximate labels would improve traceability.  Providing an explicit example of handling header-less documents would remove ambiguity.
